body: Wouldn't this be a breaking change?

Personally I see it as a bug fix, since the current behavior is not as
documented or expected.

On Fri, Mar 11, 2016, 12:37 alberto notifications@github.com wrote:

> Wouldn't this be a breaking change?
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/5547#issuecomment-195471143.
I just realized that if `--no-ignore` ignores `.eslintignore` files, it won't be possible to uningnore anything at the same time :sweat_smile:
@alberto Is that really so, given one could specify ignore patterns in the CLI using `--ignore-pattern`?
`--no-ignore` is mostly used for testing purposes (at least, that's why it was added, IIRC). I agree, this seems like a bug that was leftover after the ignore file refactoring.
@platinumazure not very intuitive, but :+1: given the context.

Unfortunately it looks like https://github.com/eslint/eslint/pull/5648 did not fully fix this issue.  It addressed it inside of `ignored-paths.js`, but we also do some checking for `options.ignore` in `cli-engine.js` in [isPathIgnored()](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/866743150898bf109efa3cb320a18b444f9683d4/lib/cli-engine.js#L695) and [executeOnText()](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/866743150898bf109efa3cb320a18b444f9683d4/lib/cli-engine.js#L658).

Testing manually on the cli reveals that `--no-ignore` still causes `node_modules` to be linted as before.
So this would only affect people using the API?
The fix only was made in `ignored-paths`, which caused its own tests to pass.  The ESLint API and CLI are still broken.
Ooops, sorry. I would swear I had also manually tested it... :(

**What version of ESLint are you using?**

`"eslint": "^2.5.1"`

**What parser (default, Babel-ESLint, etc.) are you using?**

`"babel-eslint": "^6.0.0"`

**Please show your full configuration:**

```
{
  "parser"  : "babel-eslint",
  "env"     : {
    "browser" : true
  },
  "globals" : {
    "__DEV__"      : false,
    "__PROD__"     : false,
    "__DEBUG__"    : false,
    "__DEBUG_NEW_WINDOW__" : false,
    "__BASENAME__" : false
  },
  "rules": {
    "semi": [2, "always", {"omitLastInOneLineBlock": true}],
    "comma-dangle": [2, "always-multiline"],
    "jsx-quotes": [2, "prefer-double"],
    "space-before-function-paren": [2, "never"],
    "block-spacing": [2, "never"]
  }
}
```

**What did you do? Please include the actual source code causing the issue.**

Run `eslint . ./`.

**What did you expect to happen?**

Ignore `node_modules` and lint files in other directories.

**What actually happened? Please include the actual, raw output from ESLint.**

It doesn't ignore `node_modules` and throws the following errors for every .js file in my project:

```
  1:1  error  Rule 'no-empty-label' was removed and replaced by: no-labels                 no-empty-label
  1:1  error  Rule 'space-after-keywords' was removed and replaced by: keyword-spacing     space-after-keywords
  1:1  error  Rule 'space-before-keywords' was removed and replaced by: keyword-spacing    space-before-keywords
  1:1  error  Rule 'space-return-throw-case' was removed and replaced by: keyword-spacing  space-return-throw-case
```

I don't have such rules anywhere except `node_modules`. Checked with "Find text in files" in Total Commander to make sure.

issue.body:

since JavaScript config files are supported now, can you please consider adding a (at least optional) way to ask `eslint` to lint also hidden/dot files (e.g. `.eslintrc.js` or `.eslintrc.json` with the JSON plugin) if a name to a directory is passed (e.g. `eslint .`)?
